subject: Audit header pseudonymization — PoC scope & questions
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Nina Kapoor <nina.kapoor@carevantage.com>, Daniel Cook <daniel.cook@carevantage.com>
Cc: CareVantage Security <security@carevantage.com>
Date: 2028-04-17T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Audit header pseudonymization — PoC scope & questions

Hi Nina / Daniel —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a proposed minimal PoC to validate our approach for removing or pseudonymizing sensitive headers from request/response logs while preserving debugability for your engineering team. Attached: POC-scope.pdf and a short CSV of sample headers we discussed.

Summary of what we heard from your side:
- Authorization and Cookie headers must never be retained in plaintext.
- Trace IDs are used for correlating flows across services; you prefer stable but non-reversible identifiers if possible.
- Logs must remain in US-only residency and be retained for 30 days for debugging, then purged.

Proposed PoC (high level):
1) Ingest a small, timeboxed stream (48–72h) of representative request/response logs (we can accept obfuscated payloads).
2) Apply two-tier redaction: full removal for high-risk fields (Auth, Set-Cookie), pseudonymization for trace IDs (HMAC with per-customer salt, stable for 30 days).
3) Produce side-by-side outputs: original (redacted) + sanitized view + mapping counts (no raw mapping exported).
4) Measure impact on latency, storage, and ability to correlate sessions (developer debugging checklist).

Questions for you before we lock scope:
- Can you confirm the exact list of headers you want removed vs pseudonymized? I attached a starter CSV; please annotate.
- Is HMAC-with-salt acceptable for trace IDs, or do you need a reversible token?
- Can we store the per-customer salt in KMS (we will use customer-specific keying)?

Next steps if this looks good: sign off on the attached PoC-scope, share a 48–72h sample (obfuscated) via your secure transfer, and we’ll schedule a 2-week PoC with a mid-point check.

Thanks —
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com

From: Nina Kapoor <nina.kapoor@carevantage.com>

Cc: Daniel Cook <daniel.cook@carevantage.com>, CareVantage Security <security@carevantage.com>
Date: 2028-04-17T17:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Audit header pseudonymization — PoC scope & questions

Alex —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from Security/Platform after the call:

- Authorization (all bearer tokens) and Cookie/Set-Cookie must be removed entirely from any persisted log.
- We can accept hashed/pseudonymized trace IDs provided the mapping is non-reversible and stable for our retention window (we asked for 30 days). Please confirm that HMAC with an access-controlled salt meets this.
- We need to confirm key management: keys must be customer-scoped and stored in a KMS that supports key rotation; can Redwood use our AWS KMS key or do you require Redwood-managed KMS?
- Data residency: confirm logs for this PoC will be processed and stored in us-east-1 only.
- Proof points: we need a short technical note on collision risk for your hashing approach and an example of the redacted output from your pipeline (no real PHI).

I’ve attached a brief checklist our security team uses — we’ll annotate once we review your sample outputs.

If we’re aligned on these points we can move forward. Also cc’ing Daniel for platform-side constraints.

—Nina
Nina Kapoor
Director, Engineering Ops | CareVantage Health Systems
[Attachment: CV-security-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Nina Kapoor <nina.kapoor@carevantage.com>, Daniel Cook <daniel.cook@carevantage.com>
Cc: CareVantage Security <security@carevantage.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-18T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Audit header pseudonymization — PoC scope & questions

On Tue, Apr 17, 2028 at 2:03 PM Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Nina / Daniel —
>
> Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a proposed minimal PoC ...

Nina — thanks for the fast feedback. Below are direct answers and a short proposal to address the proof points you asked for.

1) Removal vs pseudonymization
- We will fully strip Authorization, Cookie, and Set-Cookie headers from persisted logs. These fields will be zeroed in the sanitized output.

2) Trace ID approach
- Proposal: HMAC-SHA256(trace_id, customer_salt) truncated to 128 bits.
- Properties: non-reversible (no raw trace recovery), stable across calls while salt is valid, and collision probability < 2^-128 for realistic ID distributions. We will provide a short note with math and test vectors.

3) Key management / KMS
- We can support either: (a) Redwood-managed key in our KMS (with strict RBAC and audit logs) or (b) customer-managed key in your AWS KMS via key policy grant. If you prefer (b) we’ll provide integration steps.

4) Residency
- PoC processing and storage will be confined to us-east-1. We will not replicate to other regions for this engagement.

5) Proof outputs
- Attached: redaction-playbook.docx (contains sanitized example outputs and developer debugging checklist). We will also emit a short CSV that summarizes mapping stability (counts only, no raw mappings).

Proposed timeline once you sign the PoC scope:
- Week 0: transfer obfuscated 48–72h sample and exchange KMS details
- Week 1: deploy redaction pipeline to a dedicated PoC tenant; run validation tests and share sanitized outputs
- Week 2: review results, adjust rules, agree on production rollout path

Next actions for you: confirm acceptance of HMAC truncation approach and whether you want Redwood-managed or customer-managed KMS. If you approve, we’ll provision a PoC tenant and send a secure upload link.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com
